Microsoft Desktop 3000 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse I bought this set for a computer that is used for entertainment purposes only. For this, it is a great set. The keyboard is good, but the mouse is huge. As near as I can tell, it is a 5000 series mouse. But it is HUGE. Does not fit my hand well, and the side buttons are small and not placed well. Beyond that, the movement of the mouse is odd. It seems to take much more movement on my part to get the cursor where I want it to be. I have a 5000 mouse that I use on another system, and it is much slimmer, the buttons are larger and are placed perfectly. And it magnifies my hand movement as it should. I don't know why MS decided to make the mouse in this set so big and the buttons so small. All in all, it is functional and suits the purpose. If it were on a system that was used for daily work, I would not recommend it.

11/11/2016
Update. The mouse, with VERY LITTLE use, is now erratic in behavior. Especially scrolling. It will actually scroll backward on a forward roll of the wheel until it seems to catch up with itself. Not what I would expect from a Microsoft product. But they don't make it, they just design it, and obviously don't care about quality control over their product in this instance. The mouse and receiver dongle are less than three feet apart. No excuse for any lag or miscommunication.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Desktop 3000 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37 Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

One thing I sadly use a lot of – phone/USB cables for charging and data transfer. These are almost as bad as the AUX cables for my car and iPod.

So, seeing this was a Philips one – I honestly thought I lucked out. I was going to give my old cable to my mom as hers was cracking near the "C" port. I figured I could use this one - she could have my old one.

It is a DURABLE cable and looked like it would go through quite a bit. The length is perfect for charging with an adapter connected to a power strip on the floor. And, it can also plug into the USB ports on a computer (or so equipped power strip).

So, why a one star rating?

This does not work. I tried with my phone and my mom’s phone. NADA. Nothing. I tried connecting it to the adapter – nothing. Tried using just the USB cable to a USB port on a power strip (which was on since it is powering my computer) – NOTHING.

So, I tried using a USB port on my computer. NOTHING. Tried with a “USB hub” connected to my computer. There was a slight problem. The “buttons” on the port light up when a port is turned on. Despite the port for this cord being on – the lights didn’t light up. Other items connected – my external mouse and a USB flash drive – they were turned off when this cord was connected.

Needless to say – this is BELOW one star. It doesn’t even work. But, I do have to rate it something.

I could’ve gotten a bad cable – after all, there is no damage to it or the packaging. But, it still doesn't work. But, I can’t return it since it was free.
text_fidelity_b: PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37

I tried taking notes at school on it - but went back to paper. I can flip back and forth in a notebook all day, but using the Sync in class had me thumbing through old notes on my phone - which isn't encouraged.

2) it comes with a very short USB 3.0 cable, which is just what I want with a portable drive--I don't want to pack a longer-than-I need cable or have one tangled up near my laptop

3) it's very quiet

4) it's backward USB 2.0 compatible

5) The USB 3 is noticeably faster--consistently about 2.5 times as fast as the 2.0

6) it's a bit heavier than my other portables save my Prestige, but not hugely so and it feels more sturdy than several of them

7) It doesn't say so, but it's quickly and easily formatted to work on Macs--took me under a minute with Disk Utility (erase/MacOs journaled--though you have other options) and I was copying over files with no problem

will update if any issues, but right now it's a winner

text_fidelity_a:
Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black The KONNEK STEIN True Wireless Earbuds are a decent set of wireless earbuds. The sound quality is good, I’ve been using them with music and streaming shows, and I haven’t been disappointed with the sound quality.

I’m not as pleased with the short battery life, touch controls, and lack of audio cues.

I get about 2-3 hours of playback per charge. It’s rare for me to battery drain earbuds, but with this pair, I hear the low battery chime every time I use them.

The touch controls and lack of audio cues go together. The touch controls are super easy to activate on accident. More than once I’ve taken the earbuds out only to find I hit Play while doing so, and they kept playing music. I also activate random controls when adjusting the earbuds in my ears … and I don’t always know what I’ve done. Did I turn ANC on or off? The audio cues are just beeps, not an announcement like “ANC on/ANC off.”

I like the design of the case. It has a sliding top, so you can actually clean the entire area where the earbuds sit. When you put the earbuds inside the case, a light flashes to show their battery level. The case charges wirelessly or via USB-C. There’s only one LED light on the outside of the case, it’s easy to miss when you’re trying to see if the case is charging or not.
text_fidelity_b: Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EOS Rebel T3i Digital SLR Camera with EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS Lens (discontinued by manufacturer) **Please note that this review was written by a novice photographer.
I have been asking my husband for a camera for years. You know how it is....the entire time he is taking pictures with his Nikon D80 (he fancies himself a fantastic photographer...and he is), I am constantly in his ear telling how what I see and envision would make a better picture. I also tell him how he should take a picture of something that I believe will make him the next Ansel Adams. And I complete the photo shoot with, "if only I had really good camera, I would"..... Well, I guess he was tired of hearing it, and decided to buy me this camera (for Christmas thru Amazon) if for no other reason than to shut me up. I guess it was his way of putting "his" money where "my" mouth is, and I was delighted.

Now what is there to like about this camera.
-This camera is user friendly and great for a beginner photographer or at least one that is ready to move from a camera like a Nikon CoolPix. It is perfect for still shots and video (HD). It is easy to select a setting (portrait, action, etc), point and shoot. It focuses automatically (press halfway) and can be manually adjusted (tight or far away photos). There is a menu that allows you to edit and even make images, black and white. **Please note that this is the one feature that no matter how much I read the manual, I can't quite get it to do what I would like. I can edit a picture, change it to black & white, and even use the zoom tool, but when I attempt to save it, it won't. That is a feature that I will have to continue to fool with. And if anyone can help me, I would appreciate it.
-You can manipulate the viewing screen...it flips out and turns (for use while recording video) so that you can view it. Or you can swivel, flip and turn the screen around and collapse it against the body of the camera. This allows you to see or view the pictures you are taking or have taken.
- This camera takes crisp/clear photos. They are amazingly clear.
-This camera has a continuously shoot feature/function. It is great for my son's wrestling matches.
-This camera has an automatic flash that is useful if you aren't sure about the lighting.
-This camera is light (weight wise) enough to carry around for a long period of time (your hand won't get tired), but it also comes with a comfortable and adjustable neck strap. There are also cords that come with the camera so that you can use with the computer or TV.
-The battery life is decent. I assume that it also depends on how many videos you do versus still shots. However, I have done both and found and didn't have a problem. This camera also comes with a convenient battery charger.
Overall, I love my new Canon Rebel T3i and look forward to (a) learning everything about it that I can and (2) taking tons of fantastic pictures for years to come.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EOS Rebel T3i Digital SLR Camera with EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS Lens (discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model) I am using this TV as my primary PC monitor. Since I don't have my PC stationed at a desk but rather use a wireless keyboard and mouse to remotely sit where I want to, the screen can be on my wall and I can comfortably sit back in my La-Z-Boy recliner several feet away while doing work, surfing the web, gaming, or whatever. This screen is really perfect for this, with a 120 hertz rate and 4k graphics. And of course it still maintains all the regular functionality of a TV as well.

I primarily use my computer to illustrate books for my day job, and this screen really makes my illustrations look great! Set to "Graphics" mode (rather than "Entertain" mode) the colors are true and the shadows retain great detail; the highlights are smooth, and clean. The color profile is easy to adjust. I really appreciate all of this very much. In the "Entertain" mode, the colors are amped up and the graphics are sharpened, etc. This is nice for watching films and gaming, but for doing graphics work it's absolutely necessary to have the colors and details represented accurately. The excellent anti-reflection and anti-glare features are also extremely helpful in this regard.

The native speakers are about what you would expect; they aren't amazing, but they aren't really all that bad for what this TV is intended to be either. It's really all about the screen. I personally don't care too much about the speakers, because 95% of the time that I use the screen I'm wearing headphones anyway so that I don't disturb my family. But if you're a real audiophile and that sort of thing is important to you, I would suggest you get some nice speakers to go with the TV, because the built-in speakers are clearly only meant to be just good enough to pass muster, and aren't anything to be wowed by.

For me, it's really nice that it doubles as a picture frame when I'm not actively using it for anything else. I have loaded an assortment of my own favorite photographs and illustrations for it to cycle through, and they look really great on this screen, but you can also access a fairly good assortment of art through the TV itself. This turns what is typically a bit of an eyesore in my opinion (I don't like the intrusive look of too much electronic technology in my home) into a lovely, active decoration instead.

I have not ordered a decorative frame to customize it; the reviews on those seem to indicate that they are perhaps overpriced and fragile, and I think it would be easy enough to make my own anyway, which I plan to do. I think having a frame on it would just be the cherry on top, so to speak.

And to reassure anyone who is wondering about the review that said this is the 2021 model, I think there must have been some confusion on one end or the other, because I definitely received the 2022 model that I ordered.

It came with the "Slim-Fit Wall Mount" included in the box (it's in the Styrofoam packing; I think another reviewer might have just not seen it, as it's not very large and it weighs much less than you might expect) along with a decent length of "One Invisible Connection" cable to attach it to the "One Connect Box" controller. This cable is just silver braid with a clear coating on it to help it blend in better than a regular black plastic cable. It serves as a power source as well as controlling the TV, so there's no bundle of unsightly cables hanging down from the screen.

The connect box replaces the usual bulk of the TV, which is what allows the screen to hang so flat on the wall like a regular picture frame. To use the TV, you'll need to position the One Connect box where you can use the remote to control it. It can be positioned anywhere so long as it's within reach of the cable. You can buy longer "One Invisible Connection" cables if necessary. The one that was included was long enough for my needs.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

Thank you Amazon. You have scored 10+
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display

StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2) Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black I don't know what to think of these headphones. The sound out of the box is terrible, just abysmal. I've never heard a more unbalanced headphone anywhere. If you can't use an eq with these headphones, stop reading and look elsewhere.

If you can use an eq in your application, you might find these headphones surprising. Once the shrill high-end is toned down and the bass and mids bumped up, you will find the sound is pretty good for a ~$60/pair. The soundstage is small, but clear and the instrument separation surpasses what I was expecting. However, boost the bass too much and you will get distortion.

A couple of weeks before buying these I heard the quad-driver version and they were simply amazing. It was like I was sitting in my own living room listening to a full surround sound setup. I've never heard spacial definition or as big a soundstage in a headphone as I did with the quad-drivers, especially IEMs. The quad-drivers are on par with $600/pair HiFiMan planars. That's why I took a chance on this much cheaper bluetooth version of a single driver.

If you don't mind playing with the eq and don't want to buy cheap knock-offs from china (these are made in china, but by the company that designed them), take a chance on these. If you just want to plug and play, buy something else. I'm still on the fence on returning them myself.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

Amazon Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" Standing Leather Origami Case (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" - 3rd Generation), Red I had the very first kindle...with a red leather first gen case. I was really excited to get the new hdx 8.9" kindle and a new red leather case. These origami cases seem like a good idea. But if you have them sitting on any kind of slightly slick surface or slightly inclined surface, it won't stand up. The function of the "origami" part is a little complicated, but the pictures help. Initially it is it very stiff and hard to "fold". After a few uses it loosens up which makes setting up the "standing" position a little easier, but it still resists the action and as I mentioned, slips. I was thinking a little rubber edge all around the case edge would help some. The case "attaches" to the kindle via magnets and turns your kindle on automatically when you open the case, off when up close it. On the up side, I definitely prefer the feel of the leather case as opposed to the plastic one. Sadly neither case really functions as it should for standing. However it will provide some protection for the glass which is a pretty good size now. In addition to the magnet set in, there is are outer power and volume buttons. They are in good locations and I have not hit them accidently. In fact those buttons are quite handy.
I just wish they'd put more thought into actual function and less into "wow this looks cool" on the stand part.
Hope this helps some. I have not found a great alternative yet, but I will keep looking and update this review if I find one.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" Standing Leather Origami Case (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" - 3rd Generation), Red

text_fidelity_a:
Audio-Technica ATH-M50xBT2 Wireless Over-Ear Headphones, Black It's "almost" (see my edit below) impossible to find a negative review of the Audio-Technica ATH-M50x Closed Back Headphones. And I have to agree. Probably the best headphones I've ever owned. They've been available now for 10 or so years. You can't get this high end quality audio anywhere else for this price point. I got an excellent deal. The headphone purchase also included 3 high quality extra items for just about the same price as the headphones alone. My package included an extra cable, a solid hard plastic carrying case, and a FiiO A1 headphone amplifier.
The headphones live up to all the positive reviews, and the extras included made for a very good total price.
I would definitely recommend this product.
Updated 2/4/2021, 4 months later.
I still love these headphones. I have to laugh when I occasionally check the customer reviews and find that most of the criticisms are based on how these headphones were purposely engineered. Let me be more specific. Some of the negative comments include:
-others around you can hear what you're listening to. Oh well. Too bad. They should probably put on their own noise cancelling headphones. Which brings me to my next point:
-they're not noise cancelling. Yup, that's right. When I did my search for headphones, I specifically did NOT want noise cancelling OR Bluetooth. Much prefer putting the money saved when not buying these options and putting it toward better cans.
-there is no microphone on the cables. Correct again. These headphones were not necessarily intended for those who want a set of cans primarily to support their cell phone addiction.
-they must be used with the company's proprietary cables to attach to the headphones. I'll take that and love it. Why? Because they twist and lock into the bottom of the can. How many times, with other headphones, have I moved too far, or stood up or whatever, and the cord would be ripped out of the cans!!
-too much bass, not enough base. Midrange too pronounced, or not enough. And they go on and on and on.
-the "best" (tongue in cheek) criticism stated that none of the included cables, nor the included adapters fit his computer. I don't know what kind of a computer this person has, but, if Bill Cosby appears in TV commercials for your computer, headphones should not be your #1 focus right now
-and finally, and I quote, "I needed to add an EQ to make them sound like I wanted them to". Precisely! These cans were designed and manufactured specifically for those who are looking for an accurate, unadulterated representation of the original recording. The way the musicians and the recording engineers intended it to sound. If one doesn't find that acceptable, and that's fine, include an EQ somewhere in the mix. As a matter of fact, I have more than my share of sound shaping hardware and software all over my system in order to tailor the music to my liking.
You need to like the sound quality reproduced through headphones and speaker systems alike. And this is very subjective. One person's likes are another person's hates, especially when it comes from those who love to sound like they "might" know what they are talking about.. I bought and returned a number of headphones because I didn't care for how they sounded. I kept these.
I do agree with one common complaint. The earpads do get uncomfortable after a while. I checked for aftermarket replacements, but many included their own negative reviews that they changed the sound quality from the originals. That's the last thing I want.
text_fidelity_b: Audio-Technica ATH-M50xBT2 Wireless Over-Ear Headphones, Black

This case comes with a few layers of foam. One of them has pre-cut squares that you can remove for a custom fit. Over all, I found this to be a rather hassle-free, economical solution. *a T-Mount for 35mm cameras,
*a 2x Barlow,
*a light-pollution filter and my polarizing filter (in original cases.

There's room enough for a few more filters (in their original cases) and maybe 3 more larger eye pieces.

Olafus Outdoor Bluetooth Speakers 2 Packs, 40W True Wireless Stereo Patio Speaker Dual Pairing Lantern Speaker, 20 Warm White LED, Rich Bass for Garden Yard Camping I was skeptical because I've used multi-point bluetooth speaker arrays before that just sort of doubled-up a mono signal to different speakers. But this appears to be using the same Bluetooth 5 protocol that wireless earbuds utilize to send a proper dual-stream (left and right) channel for true stereo sound!
I did some sound tests that play only on each channel at a time, and it performed EXACTLY as intended! They look really cool and the lights add a lot of character to an evening garden party as well. The only issue however is that they don't get as loud as other speakers I've used. They are plenty loud for any sort of indoor space, but you can't really place these at either side of a backyard and expect to hear each other at maximum volume. You need bigger DJ-style speakers for that. But if you just want some background tunes to set the mood at a get-together on an average sized porch or deck, these are very nice and don't require any electrical outlet nearby.
I like them and intend to to use them more as the warm weather sets in.
text_fidelity_b: Olafus Outdoor Bluetooth Speakers 2 Packs, 40W True Wireless Stereo Patio Speaker Dual Pairing Lantern Speaker, 20 Warm White LED, Rich Bass for Garden Yard Camping

text_fidelity_a:
eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.
text_fidelity_b: eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert

text_fidelity_a:
Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable I ordered the 'Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts and experiences.
First off, out of the box this Bluetooth Wireless Speaker not only looks interesting but it is beautiful. I say interesting because I have never had a Wireless Speaker like this, and I wonder where would I use it and would it be practical. Well after some time with this device I must first report that it really does sound amazing. The sound is clean and immersive. It is hard to describe the incredible sound sensation while wearing it. It is almost as if you have speakers floating on either side of your head (pointing directly to your ears) and it is nothing like I have experienced before but it is pretty cool. I have been trying to think of how this Speaker would actually fit into my life. It's not like you are wearing headphones that only you can hear. While wearing this speaker, everyone else around you can hear it too but it's just not as immersive as it is to you. It's hard to describe, but what I will say is that it really is an incredible experience. If the volume is down low you can still hear your surroundings yet when you crank it up, surprisingly your surrounding sounds seem to disappear. Personally I have decided that this would be best worn while alone in your home while doing simple household chores. Like doing dishes or folding laundry. The Nomodo U speaker stays put pretty well for the most part due to the rubber neck pad, yet if you are constantly bending over or doing anything where you are moving around a lot and twisting your head and body, it tends to need re adjusted. Sitting in bed listening to Music or listening to an audio book works really well with this device as long as you wont be disturbing your partner. As for watching movies, for me this really doesn't work. I can't find anywhere where it says what version of Bluetooth this is using but I don't think it is Bluetooth 5.0 unfortunately. There are noticeable sync issues and this just gets annoying. Speaking of the Bluetooth, it connects/pairs effortlessly to all of my devices and that is a bonus. I am disappointed however that it uses Micro USB (the cable is included btw) for charging. With this being a new device it should have USB Type C. I always have to mention this with any new devices. Call quality is acceptable. Those on the other end can hear you just fine, as long as you are not in a loud environment. This is pretty typical with most wireless headphones. Overall I do love this device and think it is a great value for what it is.
text_fidelity_b: Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable

I used a dB meter that was about 6ft away with the speaker pointed towards the meter. At max volume on my main phone (fold3) and at 150% volume, I was getting a consistent mid-90s dB for melody and lyrics, with peaks up to 109dB. On my other device (Note 10+), also at 150%, it was pulling about 70 dB on TV dialogue. I did try testing it with a volume booster, and even with only 110% (on top of the 150%) it was beginning to distort.
I played the TV audio for about 16hrs at moderate and 8hrs on low, and it was reading as still having 70% battery. But after only a few hours of moderate-high volume music, that 70% was gone and it died.
The sound quality is quite good with a warm tone. The highs are clear and the bass is better than I expected for there not to be a dedicated bass cone.
Despite appearances, I think the best use for this will be background music - not too loud will keep it playing all day & night and it will provide a much cleaner and richer sound than a small speaker at similar volume.
text_fidelity_b: BUGANI Bluetooth Speakers, M83 Speaker IPX6 Waterproof Portable LargeWireless Speaker,Bluetooth 5.2, Wireless Two Pairing,24H Playtime,Suitable for Family Gatherings and Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker

Onkyo HT-S5100 7.1 Channel Home Entertainment System (Set of Nine, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The Onkyo HT-S5100 Home Entertainment System sounded quite good when listening to the radio, and I really loved the self-calibration feature to set the speaker phase/power-level based upon our optimum seating position.

When the receiver is played at low to mid volume ranges, the system was impressive, but there was distoration at higher levels when the speakers were driven beyond their capabilities.

As far as a Stereo Receiver goes, I'd give it high marks, but as far as a Home Entertainment system goes... in my opinion, I'd purchase something else.

I found after many frustrating hours of trying to get the receiver to work with my other HDMI components, that all of my attempts were in vain.

I'd essentially purchased the system on the recommedation of Consumer Reports (They crowed about the HT-S5100 having the best sound of any system they'd ever tested, and it was one of the only ones offering 7.1 versus 5.1 stereo surround).

I eventually re-read the Onkyo Owners Manual and found a small blurb regarding the audio of the system not working with HDMI...

I freely admit I'd blown-off the fact that analog/digital connectors were shown on the Quick Hook-Up illustrations (thinking these were alternative connections for those unlucky soul's who didn't have HDMI), when I finally resorted to contacting Onkyo for assistance/confirmation.

They confirmed my worst-fear, their HDMI's were (Pass-Though). When asked why they even bothered to put HDMI connectors on the system, the reply was (some consumers desired them).

Personally, I feel if a system has HDMI connectors present, that is implies they're fully compliant, otherwise their presence is misleading.

What this meant was all of my new toy's (50" Plasma, Blu-ray player, and Xbox 360) could only pass on video (not the higher quality audio signals through the HDMI connectors), and that I'd have to accept a lower quality audio output due to the use of standard audio connectors.

Perhaps I'd missed this in CR's review (or it wasn't stated), as I had to purchase additional digital cabling so that I could even hear the audio content of the devices hooked into the Onkyo (added expense/wiring woe's).

If I had to do it all over again, I'd purchase the HT-S5100 as a Stereo Receiver, but I wouldn't recommend it as the hub for a Home Entertainment System to interconnect your HDMI devices.

Another pearl-of-wisdom, don't rely strictly upon the written advice of a third-party, go out and listen/view the equipment yourself, as that's what I'm wishing I'd have done!
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo HT-S5100 7.1 Channel Home Entertainment System (Set of Nine, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HT-A5000 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos Sound Bar Surround Sound Home Theater with DTS:X and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, works with Alexa and Google Assistant,Black This arrived well packaged and without issues. I've tried out several major brand soundbars in recent years, and I've yet to find any that are as good as the Sonys, at least as a television speaker. I've already got an A7000 that I'm familiar with to compare this A5000 with. It's a step down in price and feature set, but there's more to the differences than that.

The A7000 has cloth speaker covers on top, while this A5000 has plastic. It's my impression that the sound is a bit better out of the cloth, since it provides less of a reflective barrier, but it's also hard to keep clean and safe. Being on top of the speaker facing up, it's right where something can get pur or dropped on it, or a cat walking across it. The hard plastic seems much more resilient. It's also hard to tell on the sound, because the A5000 has two fewer speakers.

The top of this speaker is a textured plastic, like a car's dashboard. Not super fancy, but resilient. The A7000 has very shiny black plastic, which looks very nice and is easy to clean, but also lacks resilience and shows dust more readily.

The remote is infrared, so you need to have line of sight to the speaker for it to work, but it's full featured, even having buttons to control optional additional speakers. which I really appreciate.

The instruction book is pretty good. Setup is easy, especially if you connect it to a television. It'll put the menus right up on the screen. It's really built to be a television speaker with bluetooth and other inputs so it can be used for other things as a secondary purpose.

I'm still trying to figure out what I can do with the Chromecast feature that seems to be present in the speaker, but not in the television. So far I haven't had much luck connecting with Chromecast.

I definitely like the A7000 better, but there's a solid price difference. I love having a second HDMI input, since the way they've got these things set up, it outputs to my Sony television rather than the other way around, so I need to plug in extra devices to the soundbar, not the television, which makes it a weird decision to put so many more ports on the television than the speaker.

Great speaker, but still plenty of things that could be improved in a future version, like more satellite speaker compatibility, some kind of port passthrough from television, chromecast video, etc.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HT-A5000 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos Sound Bar Surround Sound Home Theater with DTS:X and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, works with Alexa and Google Assistant,Black

text_fidelity_a: Rankie DisplayPort (DP) to HDMI Adapter, 4K Resolution Ready Converter with Audio (Black) I would have given this five stars, except that 1) I purchased it July 23, 2016 and 2) on October 1, 2016, it failed.  I'd noticed that my monitor was extremely susceptible to static interference, where my other two monitors (not using this adapter) were not.  Tonight it just quit working altogether.  I checked the connections on the back of the monitor, all were fine.  I then checked the connection to the graphics card (NVidia gtx 1060), which is what I used this adapter for.  Unfortunately, when I attempted to pull the adapter out of the graphics card, the adapter came apart in pieces, leaving the end part in the HDMI port in the graphics card.  I've attached photos to show.  I could not take the piece out of the graphics card with my bare hands.  I had to completely shut down my computer and use pliers, held on each side (left and right side, as top/bottom pinch type grip didn't work), and pull with all of my might to remove the piece out of the computer.  I couldn't believe this thing.  I will never use this product again and suggest you find a product with a more reliable name/more reliability in general.  I hope this port on my graphics card isn't destroyed!!!!
text_fidelity_b: Rankie DisplayPort (DP) to HDMI Adapter, 4K Resolution Ready Converter with Audio (Black)

turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus I received a review copy of this receiver and put it through its paces. I am going to compare it to a receiver that I've owned since 2011 and have been thoroughly pleased with: [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]].

It's a complete solution: the box contained easy-to-follow instructions and two sets of cables: one 3.5mm male at each end and the other with a 3.5mm male splitting into two RCA males. Those are a nice touch because some speakers require one or the other. With my Belkin I had to purchase an adapter to use it with one of my powered speakers. So having a complete solution right out of the box is a plus.

The receiver looks like a wall wart that plugs directly into a wall socket. It's about two inches tall and 1.75 inches wide, so it does eat up come space. Since the speaker cable comes out the bottom of the device you are pretty much locked into plugging it into the bottom receptacle.

One feature I loved is this also has a port for USB charging that allows you to keep your phone or MP3 player fully charged while playing music.

This, of course, is based on later technology and it shows. I greatly exceeded the ten meter distance limit by taking my phone to the opposite end of my house, two rooms apart from the receiver, and still managed a clear signal. Believe me, on its best day the Belkin struggled to receive a line of sight signal within a ten meter limit. I even took my phone outside and could hear clear reception coming from my speakers inside my house.

While the instruction sheet will step you through connecting to and using this receiver I did not bother to read it. I opened the bluetooth settings on my [[ASIN:B00AB7FVCY Samsung Galaxy Note II]], scanned for new devices and when BrightPlay Home showed up in the list I tapped it to connect and started streaming music to my speaker. It took longer to unpackage the receiver than it did to start using it. It does not get any easier.

The sound quality is markedly better too. I switched back and forth between the Belkin receiver and this one - attached to the same powered speakers - and could tell the difference. Not by much, mind you, but it's discernible. I had a friend listen and she agreed.

Overall this is an excellent receiver that exceeded the recommended specs in the instruction sheet and it a breeze to use. If I had to replace this it would be with an identical receiver and that is the highest praise I can bestow.
text_fidelity_b: turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 900VA UPS Desktop Battery Back Up, 12 Outlet, 480W 120V Standby, Ultra-Compact, USB (INTERNET900U) First off, this was purchased for a 27" iMac for home usage.

I changed my previous configuration where my modem, router, NAS and iMac were all located in or on my office desk. These were all connected to a CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD that's been working perfectly for almost 5 years. After moving the location of the modem, router and NAS to a more central location; I moved the CyberPower UPS along with them. This left me for a need for a small UPS for the iMac only.

I originally looked at the smaller Cyberpower UPSs but then looked at the competition. The two I had narrowed it down to were similar in price, but the Tripp Lite offered a larger battery capacity. I then looked at their listings and found the Origin listed under the Product Information. The Tripp LIte stated that it was Made in USA or Imported while the Cyberpower was listed with a China origin. A little more searching and Tripp Lite is based out of Chicago. This essentially sealed the deal and the INTERNET 550U was ordered from Amazon.

Much to my disappointment, there was a large label on the side of the box clearly stating MADE IN CHINA. -1 Star

From the Manufacturer section of the listing would have you believe that the PowerAlert Software will work on the Mac OSX. After trying to find the PowerAlert Software from the Trip Lite web site would state the following...

"If you are a home or small office user, PowerAlert Local is for you. It allows you to monitor and control a UPS system connected to your computer through a USB or serial cable. It also supports automatic file saves and unattended computer shutdown during power outages."

Looking below this statement and there is no download availability for Mac OSX. The only Mac OSX software availability is called PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent and it states the following...

"If you need to automate computer shutdown during an outage without a USB or serial connection to a UPS system, or if you can’t use Java, PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent is for you. When it detects a user-selected event (such as low battery) broadcast by a network-connected UPS system, it initiates shutdown or hibernation after a user-defined delay."

Not quite what I was looking for but I did find that the native software within Mac OSX seems to do what I need it to do without the need of installing additional software. -0 Stars

This UPS is considerably light compared to the larger CyberPower. For whatever reason, I was expecting something heavier. It gives the impression that it's cheap in feel. Not necessarily of any fault of the device but some perceived notion that I had. But when coupled with the horrible, plastic smell; it comes off as another characteristic of a cheap, Chinese product. -1 Star

In summary, we had a long power outage last weekend while I was at the computer. The UPS worked as it should, allowing me to shut down the computer.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 900VA UPS Desktop Battery Back Up, 12 Outlet, 480W 120V Standby, Ultra-Compact, USB (INTERNET900U)

A great feature is that you can copy music files to the earbuds. They have 4GB of built-in storage. This means you don’t have to stay within Bluetooth range of your mobile device to play music.

Three stars because I haven’t used the earbuds consistently for a full month. As much as I love these, I’m afraid that the left earbud will fail before long (as other reviewers have reported).

Already the left earbud has exhibited signs of NOT charging properly. With the case closed and plugged in (and with brand-new earbuds), the left charging light blinked red, which indicates “not charging”. I corrected the problem by opening the case and reseating the left earbud in the cradle, but of course I’m wondering whether there is a more serious problem that will surface soon.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers I tried the first generation Kindle but didn't really care all that much for it. While I loved the screen, it just didn't feel right, and remember thinking this would be perfect if it had a touchscreen.

When the Touch was announced I ordered this along with a Fire with the thought that the Fire would be for me, and I'd give the Touch as a gift. The Touch got here this morning and I opened it up just to make sure it was OK. It looked so nice that I carefully peeled off the plastic just to try it out for a few minutes. After all, one wouldn't want to give a gift that didn't work, right? Well, it's now been a few hours and several chapters of a few books later. I'm keeping it. A second one will be on order for Christmas giving.

Why keep the Touch when I also have a Fire? If you skip over the obvious answer (I just love electronic gadgets) the e-ink on the Touch is much better in terms of clarity and lack of glare. Not that the Fire is bad. It has a very clear screen, but there is some glare. The Touch is better for reading under all lighting situations, and remains highly readable in direct sun. I can't imagine getting better screen clarity than this for black and white text.

I also tried reading it while on a treadmill (a situation that usually gives me a headache when I tried it using the kindle app on my Touchpad) and it was quite pleasant. Best of all is that I can zoom up the text size so I can read it while it is on the treadmill reading stand (it's too far away for me to read hard copy unless it's in HUGE type. Getting old is _not_ fun).

But the strength of the Touch is also it's biggest problem for me - black and white. I read several magazines each month and reading them in B/W is lackluster at best. Magazines are more enjoyable on the Fire, especially publications such as Wired.

The touch interface is great. So far its been very smooth and glitch free. Love the feel of the screen - has a bit of texture to it. I have to say, however, that I am a bit concerned about the screen longevity. The Touch overall feels a bit fragile and less "solid" than the Fire. I'm not deducting any stars for that since it's just an impression, but it will be interesting to see if the durability of the Touch screen is better/worse/same as the Fire (and vice versa). I'll be getting a case for it for sure since it's going to be getting bumped about.

I'll be using the Fire mainly at home and for reading material that works best in color (and, of course, video - need to relax the mind with mindless entertainment as well!). The Touch will be living in my briefcase for reading while commuting (I take the bus and subway, so lots of time to read) and for killing time prior to an appointment. The longer battery life and smaller size makes it a better traveling companion than the Fire. I don't have the Touch 3G version, so I'll have to make sure I keep a few books on my to-be-read stack so I don't run out when I'm out of wi-fi range.

Granted, if I could only have one device, I'd stay with the Fire since that offers more entertainment options, albeit at twice the price. But the cost is not excessive, so I treated myself to both. With a Fire and a Touch I've got all bases covered (until, of course, the next glittery gee-whiz piece of electronics comes out...).

text_fidelity_a: Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 1 TB USB 2.0 External Hard Drive STAC1000100 (Black) I'm one of the folks who had a hard drive crash without having backed up for several months.  That was all it took for me to realize the importance of backing up my hard drive regularly and not simply putting current files on a flash drive.  I'd been using a Western Digital drive for the past three or four years, then was told that hard drives have a limited life span.  That made sense, so I decided to replace the external drive which is used to backup my MacBook.  I almost purchased the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex 500 GB USB 2.0 Ultra-Portable External Hard Drive STAA500100, then decided that I don't take the external drive with me and didn't need it to be portable.  Enter the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 2 TB Desktop External Hard Drive STAC2000100, a shiny black drive that looks much sleeker and way more shiny than the dull Western Digital.  2 TB seemed like more than I need, but I went for it anyway.  Before the package arrived, I watched the videos available on the Seagate website, so I was prepared for this drive and felt comfortable using it as my new backup drive.  My only question was whether or not to format it for use with Mac and PC or just the Mac.  Decided on the Mac only and didn't install the other options onto my MacBook.  Since I use Time Machine, I immediately proceeded to backup the hard drive.  Not having purchased the optional Firewire, eSATA or USB 3.0, the transfer is not faster than on the other external drives I've used, but this one sure is quiet and it's much nicer to look at.  It also doesn't weigh as much as other desktop external drives.  Looks like the attractive Seagate sleek shape, just bigger.  There is no button to push, just plug in and connect, then go to Time Machine.  I cannot review the included Memeo backup because I've not installed it.  Can't imagine that it would be better than Time Machine.  This meets my needs and exceeds my expectations.  It also looks nicer when locked up in my fire retardant portable safe than any other drive.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 1 TB USB 2.0 External Hard Drive STAC1000100 (Black)

Bose QuietComfort Noise Cancelling Earbuds-Bluetooth Wireless Earphones, Triple Black My family has tested out numerous noise canceling earbuds in the last six months, looking for the best ones to fit each member of our household. This set of earbuds was the universal favorite among every member of our family.

For one, the noise cancellation feature is absolutely the most effective noise cancellation we have found on earbuds. Even having it on silent, I was unable to discern individual words from my mom reading loudly to my two noisy children in the other room. With an audiobook playing, I really didn't notice anybody else being in the house, though I could hear them if I thought about it. With music, it was like they weren't there, someone can stand right next to me and talk to me and I can be blissfully unaware.

If you get overloaded from auditory stimulation easily and just need the world to stop making so much noise every so often, these are the earbuds to get.

The sound quality is extraordinarily good on audiobooks, rap music, metal music, and more peaceful and soothing ballads and classical. The base was not overwhelming, nor did the treble get screechy.

It fit my very small ears well, and fit my husband's ears well also, he has a much bigger ear canal size.

The one thing that we have both noticed is that these are also heavier than most of our other earbuds, however even with my ears feeling rather sensitive, it really didn't bother me because they are weighted nicely and fit so well.

Overall, while these could be improved by being slightly smaller and less heavy, these still beat out five other well-known brands in our household for both the noise cancellation and in audio quality.

Samsung Galaxy Tab (7-inch, 16GB, Wi-Fi) I really liked this 7" Tab (GT-P1010) at first. It's most useful function is web surfing.

Now, after several months of use, it's SLOOOOOOOW to load and update pages and locks up occasionally for no particular reason. I've uninstalled every unnecessary app but whether using the default Browser or Dolphin, it's more frustrating than useful.

It's also inaccurate for when inputting via keyboard. Oftentimes the keyboard adds wild characters all by itself.

Forget firmware updates. You are stuck with whatever it came with. And if you think Samsung will be any help, think again. I put "GT-P1010" in Samsung's product support page and got "no results."

I have to say Apple's major firmware updates work a whole lot better. First, because they happen at all and second, because they are seamless and reliable. Android is buggy and needs fixing on this Samsung Tablet. Samsung's "answer" is to buy a new tablet.

The device has two cameras and would be ideal for video chatting, but won't work with Skype. Apparently it needs the next version of Android. (See above concerning that impossibility.) But who knows if the next-up model will work either?

These things all want to be Apple but simply fall short.

One nice thing is that most Flash content is supported when web surfing. Apple is way lacking here. I used an iPad 1 for some time and it's pretty frustrating that it simply ignores so much content.

Bottom line is I won't buy another wannabe Samsung device like this that lacks firmware updates. (I did the same thing looking for the perfect mp3 player: everyone tried to sell the "iPod killer" and I spent more money trying to avoid the iPod. Then I bought an iPod3 and later an iPhone4 and understood how excellent their engineering and software and OS are and how with OS updates the devices continually get better even after you make the purchase.) They are too expensive to throw away and Samsung can't or won't fix the bugs. Thus you are stuck with an expensive, buggy toy that's frustrating to use. No thank you.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab (7-inch, 16GB, Wi-Fi)

D-Link DWL-800AP+ Wireless Range Extender, 802.11b, 22Mbps My need for this device was to extend signal strength in my new home. I recently moved from California where houses are basically wood framed, to a new, larger home in Florida where houses use blocks for outside and load bearing walls. This heavier construction, combined with the distance between my wireless router and where I use my computer, severely degraded my signal and throughput. I purchased this device to rectify that problem - which it did.
Installation, including putting it in wireless range extender mode, took mere minutes after unpacking it. I was communicating with an incredible 100% signal strength in practically no time after setting it up, which was a dramatic difference from the 20% strength before it was installed. I did an experiment by walking outside with my laptop and was still connected to my home network with 80% or better signal all the way to the end of my property.
I like the fact that this device seems to interoperate flawlessly with other vendor products. One of my systems has an SMC wireless card, and another uses a Linksys. My wireless router is an SMC.
Installation instructions were a bit sparse. I am a highly technical user, so I didn't need them, but a novice may have problems. Since I have not needed to use technical support I cannot comment on the quality of D-Link's support.
Since I have not used this device as an access point I also cannot comment on how well it works in that mode. However, if you are seeking a simple and cost-effective solution to extending the range of your existing wireless LAN, and have some technical skills this may be the solution you are looking for. Even though I am pleased with this product I rated it at four stars because I have not used all of the features or D-Link's technical support, and do not think the documentation is novice-friendly.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link DWL-800AP+ Wireless Range Extender, 802.11b, 22Mbps

text_fidelity_a:
Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100) I ended up using this colorimeter to profile and calibrate my monitor. Out of the box I was not very happy with the quality of the product. You end up getting pretty much zero instruction and no manual. I had to figure it out on my own just by looking at the product. Once that annoyance was over I got to experience how terrible the default software from datacolor is.

I looked to the reviews and decided I could make the most of this purchase by using other free calibration software. I used Argyll and DispCalGUI. If you simply download DispCalGUI it will prompt you automatically to download the Argyll color libraries.

You then go into Tools->Instrument->install Argyll CMS instrument drivers...

This will download the drivers you need to run the spyder 5.

After this calibration is possible. I calibrated and it seemed to do a decent job. All in all, the calibration software looked like it was powerful--certainly better than the default.

In the end, I returned the product. I wanted something that would work without me having to go the extra mile to get it to work. At this point, with all of the extra I had to do to calibrate I still don't know if it did a good job or not.

Dimensions can be seen in the photos I have attached.

Included is the unit only.

Pros:
*Calibrates
*Decent price

Cons:
*Terrible OEM software (-2 stars)
*Setup--while not hard--is not immediately obvious. A small pamphlet would have gone a long way (-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Go for hardware that has good software calibration tools. You cant beat the two working in synergy.

Overall: 2.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 3 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.
text_fidelity_b: Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100)

text_fidelity_a:
Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso I got the "acceptable" unit for total $17 (sorry), one foot pad is missing, I'll innovate. Firstly, I had wanted the chrome front but couldn't afford it and didn't want to wait a week; when I saw this used for the price I just pushed the button.

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".
text_fidelity_b: Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso

text_fidelity_a:
Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US) Though I am giving a review for this backpack, I can't come from the perspective of having used it for a while. I only received my Targus backpack yesterday, but from the looks of it I am pretty darn sure this backpack will last a long, long time. I've used MANY backpacks in the past carrying books, laptops and supplies during the time it took to earn two separate college degrees, and at my previous job of 17 years. I had to carry tools, manuals, laptops and assorted parts to calibrate monitoring equipment around my state. I was rough on the backpacks and some wore out.

I really wish I had had a backpack like this one. It's very well constructed out of strong materials, has a plethora of pockets and places to organize your stuff, and though I don't have a 17" notebook as of yet, it appears to be deep and wide and should easily fit one. There are even slots for file folders and inside zipper pouches. There are pockets on the inside and pockets on the outside. The bottom inside has a foam rubber "shock pad" that neatly folds down flat on the bottom of the backpack and is about 1/2" thick. Plus the bottom is covered in a waterproof rubbery material that should definitely help keep water from seeping up into the bag. That happened to me several times on my job with my other backpacks and it was really frustrating. It's very easy to set your backpack down on the ground not realizing the area is wet.

The shoulder straps are padded and adjustable, and it has a waist strap for extra stability. Even if you didn't use this backpack to tote your 17" marvel of technology around, it would serve well as a camper/hiker backpack. I can't wait to start using it. If something should go wrong or tear up, I will most definitely update this review telling about it, but for now I can find no fault whatsoever with it.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US)

I then moved it to its' present location with the idea that the antennas footprint is considerably smaller than all the satellite dishes mounted on balconies throughout the complex. The mounting bracket and pole that come with it, are the same type satellite dishes use, Very strong and versatile. You will need to buy some good bolts, I used 4, 5/16" x 1- 1/2" Galvanized Lag and flat washers, I predrilled 3/16" pilot holes first. I just thought I'd mention that for those not fastener savvy.

I would guess the antenna mount alone is worth 1/3rd of the entire antenna cost. Recommend a good quad shield coaxial cable with the thick, sollid copper wire. A shorter run is better if possible. I only have about 12 feet to my PC/TV.

Once I figured out how to mount this antenna correctly, a month ago, I haven't had to adjust it.

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This camera is yet another product made in China and sold here in the United States for prices equivalent to what we'd pay if the thing was actually made in the USA, which IT IS NOT. The plastic it's made with seems cheap and brittle.

The setup instructions are WRONG and can lead you through a lengthy hell to install and configure the camera. The camera DID NOT HAVE THE MOST CURRENT SOFTWARE and I was forced through an update TWICE because the first one was the wrong one. Yes, the wrong one was recommended on their website. It took a second pass to get the correct version. Speaking of their website, it's a real mess, difficult to navigate, impossible to locate what you need on it, and just plain annoying. Tech support is mostly via email and the one time I did get a human, he didn't know much about anything.

You may want to use the camera's web interface to set up security and so forth. The GOTCHA is the cameras use Java and Java is going to drive your internet security software, firewall and virus protection wild. Java is known to be a welcome mat announcing your computer is open for all manner of malware, virus infections and so on. My security software blocked the install entirely.

Access to the camera remotely is via the D-Link website through an account you set up. To see the camera's video you must go to the website, log in and then view the camera. As video goes from camera to the D-Link website and then to you via your mobile device, the panning and zooming is jerky due to the lag in the up and download of the signal.

If you're looking for a security camera to use while traveling, or out for an evening, this will take care of things--barely. If you want a home security system with multiple cameras, go for a dedicated system with hard-wired cameras, a DVR and a solid wall around it for security. This camera is a toy compared to industrial or home-grade security.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Lenovo IdeaPad 3 14" Laptop, 14.0" FHD 1920 x 1080 Display, AMD Ryzen 5 3500U Processor, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 256GB SSD, AMD Radeon Vega 8 Graphics, Narrow Bezel, Windows 10, 81W0003QUS, Abyss Blue I gave this to my daughter just over 5 months ago to use as her gaming computer (Minecraft, Fortnite, Among Us, Roblox). It worked BEAUTIFULLY for 5 months until one day out of nowhere, we, too, got the black screen of death that so many others have. It was still running, but the screen was black and my cursor had a spinning circle next to it. I am pretty good with computers so I tried all the usual fixes, and nothing worked. I’d always end up right back at the black screen.
BUT - I kept trying and I’m happy to report that I FIXED IT!!!

I opened a warranty claim with Lenovo & scheduled an appointment at Best Buy, but then after reading other reviews here, it was clear that this is a common problem. So I headed to YouTube. There’s a channel called PC Monkey & he has videos to walk you through all the troubleshooting for this problem. I tried all of the easy ones, but none worked. I ended up following his instructions for a fresh install of Windows from a USB - and lo and behold the laptop is like new again! It only took about 30 minutes to complete the process, and you will need another computer + a flash drive to download the install file.

I probably will not buy another Lenovo after this experience. I hope this review helps someone else who runs into the same problem.

text_fidelity_a:
Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 - (2022) - Essential Gaming Laptop Computer - 15.6" FHD - 120Hz - AMD Ryzen 5 6600H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 - 8GB DDR5 RAM - 256GB NVMe Storage - Windows 11 Home I’ve spent the last month using and playing games on the Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3. It’s a decent entry-level laptop. I wouldn’t consider it a dedicated gaming machine, but more aimed at daily use plus some gaming.

The laptop includes 3 free months of Xbox Game Pass, so I’ve played games available through that library. Games like Moonlighter, Moonglow Bay, Tunic, Sims 4, and Hades. The laptop handled all of those just fine, but many are older games and/or not very hardware intensive.

However, I don’t think 8GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD are enough. In my very first day of downloading games, I filled more than half the hard drive (and only ~236GB is available to start). As for the RAM, my 5-year-old laptop has 8GB of RAM and I’m feeling it. A laptop from 2022 should start with at least 16GB.

The Quad Vent fans vent in the back and on both sides of the laptop. I wish there wasn’t a vent on the right, because it’s right where the mouse sits. After maybe twenty to thirty minutes, my hand gets sweaty, which isn’t great when playing a competitive game.

There are 2 USB-A ports, one on each side. The back has an HDMI port, Ethernet, USB-C, and the power input. I actually really like the power input being on the back, as that way the cable isn’t in the way when using the mouse. But I’d like another USB-A port in the back, because I can see using a hub with this laptop.

The keyboard is not my favorite. On the plus side, it’s a full keyboard. I can’t remember the last time I saw a laptop with a numpad. The keyboard has backlighting, but only one color option: white. The keys are flat on top and somewhat slippery. The keyboard itself feels cramped, especially when gaming with WASD.

The laptop is heavy, about 7 or 8 pounds. It’s not something you’ll want to tote from class to class. The battery lasts about an hour if playing games, and about 3 hours for normal use.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 - (2022) - Essential Gaming Laptop Computer - 15.6" FHD - 120Hz - AMD Ryzen 5 6600H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 - 8GB DDR5 RAM - 256GB NVMe Storage - Windows 11 Home

text_fidelity_a:
Sangean H201 Portable AM/FM/Weather Alert Digital Tuning Waterproof Shower Radio White I've tried a few of the low-end shower radios, such as the sub-$10 models from companies such as Conair. The quality of those items is in line with the price tag - yes, it is a radio, but chances it will last about as long as the battery before it breaks.

A friend of mine has the Sony model, which is a big step up in quality and sound. I took a look at that but the form factor was not right. The buttons are on the top, and it is not convenient to use when mounted on the wall (which is where it would work best for my situation). The sound was pretty good, but reception was spotty.

Took a shot on the Sangean, and was really impressed from the get-go. This is one solidly-built radio! Impressive sound -- very clear and well balanced with decent bass. Outstanding reception that clearly pulls in stations that I find hard to get on any other radio in the house.

The design is excellent, with clearly labeled and easy to use buttons. They make a solid click when you push them, and feel like they will last a long time without any problems. Has a large display with backlighting that turns on automatically for about 15 seconds with any button push. It shows the station, time, battery status, and other indicators in large letters (important for a shower radio since I don't have my glasses on in the shower). Has an auto shut off that works in increments of 10 minutes, and a "nap" timer that can be programmed for any amount of time.

It uses 2 D cell batteries that add to the heft, but ensure you won't need to change batteries very often (other reviewers note that the batteries can last for years if used about 15 or so min a day. Haven't owned mine that long so I can't vouch for that yet!)

I mounted mine on the wall using the supplied bracket. It has self adhesive pads so you don't have to drill. They looked like they would be secure, but I opted to attach the bracket to the wall with screws rather than the pads. In addition to security against falls, I wanted to be able to move the radio to another spot down the road without having to deal with the mess of removing adhesive pads. It also comes with a strap so you can hang it on a hook, or hang it from the attached handle (which swivels out of the way if you don't need to use it).

If you're looking for the ultimate in shower radios, this is the only one that should be on your shopping list. Pricy, but worth every penny.

UPDATE: December 4, 2010: It's been nearly 2 years since I started using this (21 months to be exact), and still have 2 of 3 bars of battery strength. Use it about 10 min a day, every day. Still works just as well as day 1. Well worth the price charged.

UPDATE: July 19, 2012: Well, I finally had to replace the batteries. They lasted for THREE years of daily use! Wow! The radio also continues to work perfectly. Zero problems. Given that I never was able to get one of the cheap shower radios to last longer than a year, this has been a great purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Sangean H201 Portable AM/FM/Weather Alert Digital Tuning Waterproof Shower Radio White

text_fidelity_a:
D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.
text_fidelity_b: D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D)
