SABRENT USB 2.0 to DB25 IEEE 1284 Parallel Printer Cable Adapter [HEXNUT Connectors] (CB-1284) Although every new printer has a USB port, I have a few older, but still perfectly functioning printers that only have parallel inputs. I've been using those printers with PCs that have a parallel output port but, as those PCs get retired, it's getting harder to find a way to hook up the old printers. This solves that problem very well.

It's a simple cable. One end is a USB plug; the other is a DB25 female parallel port. IMPORTANT: you want to check your printer to make sure it can accept a DB25 female plug. Many printers only have a 36-pin Centronics input. If so, you need to get this one: [[ASIN:B00IDU0T1Y Sabrent USB to Parallel IEEE 1284 Printer Cable Adapter (CB-CN36)]]

The cable itself is decent. Thin, but the jacket feels more than sturdy enough for the job at hand. It's only 6 foot long which is OK for my needs but just barely. A longer version (10 or 12 foot) would be nice.

Works fine, and no complaints.
[Sample provided for review]

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Max Wireless Over-Ear Headphones. Active Noise Cancelling, Transparency Mode, Spatial Audio, Digital Crown for Volume Control. Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone - Green I see people raving up and down about the perfection and wonderfulness of these headphones; I’m not as completely blown away by them as those people are. Quality of construction does seem to be excellent (although because Amazon doesn’t lower all prices at the start of Prime Day but only lowers some of them well after Prime Day has begun, I had to send back the first pair I bought and purchase another pair to get a discounted price, and the piston things for extending and compressing the size of the headphones was smoother on the first pair I had) and they’re comfortable enough to wear for extended periods, but while it may be a limitation of Bluetooth (I don’t know), I haven’t noticed myself being amazed by their bass response. No, in fact I just now watched the video for Shake It Off and listened to a couple of Lana Del Rey tracks and these headphones are definitely lacking in bass response – as in, there’s very little, and what there is gets completely lost under any midrange and high-end sounds that may be playing at the same time. They’re tinny-sounding. I have to wonder what the people are listening to with these who are praising the sound quality so enthusiastically.

On the other hand, I don’t ordinarily listen to music anymore, but only to talks and lectures; While I’m watching movies is probably the only time I’m going to really want big bass, and I watched The Revenant last night and didn’t feel like I was missing anything…

So their construction is much more solid than that of probably most other headphones on the market, they’re comfortable to wear, and there’s a nice ecosystem of accessories out there, but I personally find the sound quality quite lacking and I’m going to have to decide whether to hang onto these or return them.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Max Wireless Over-Ear Headphones. Active Noise Cancelling, Transparency Mode, Spatial Audio, Digital Crown for Volume Control. Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone - Green

text_fidelity_a:
CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White) I purchased these for the RM650x in my new build. to clean up the appearance of my case, as the default Corsair cables are serviceable but neither flexible nor visually appealing. Do I have a fancy case? It's a Fractal Define Mini C, so, sorta. Do I have a side window? No. Will anyone ever see the interior of this case aside from me and randos and I'm flexing on? Certainly not.

Why get cables like these? Call it an eccentricity. I don't like chaos hiding right out of sight. Sure, the Mini C would have the outward appearance of a stocky monolith of unalloyed order, but inside there would be a twisting madness of PVC and copper, heaving silently against the surface. There would be no evidence of it, sure, but I would know.

I would know.

So anyway, I purchased these to extend the relentless teleology of the IC into the broader world, and to this end I was successful. The cables are much more flexible than the default ones and the paracord is an interesting contrast against the typical circuit boards and enameled aluminum panels. They are a bit pricey for what you get, that's definitely the case - you might be better served by getting a different brand or shorter extensions rather than the full PSU set. I just happened to have the money for the CableMods.

Caveats: if you are using velcro ties inside the case, then you have to be careful with the ModFlex, as the hook-side can pull threads from it. I presume ModMesh, being nylon, would not have that issue. to get around it, I used rubber/silicon bands, since unlike zipties they can be removed and adjusted relatively easily.

Would I recommend them? If you have a side-window or transparent case, they are a definitely aesthetically on point. ModFlex or ModMesh, either should be suitable. If not, unless you too are eccentric, it probably isn't worth it. The improvement in airflow and the reduction in strain on the components are minimal so long as you are implementing reasonable cable management techniques. I'm still happy I purchased them though, since I'm pretty sure I'll be able to use them in the next two-three builds and they did make it a bit easier to get everything where I wanted it.
text_fidelity_b: CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White)

When I had the family fifteen year old listen to them though, he thought the dialogue came through just fine. So the issue was my old guy ears, not anything to do with the speakers. All and all, they really do have a nice sound for the price.

To talk about the quality of the speakers' construction, let me make a distinction between cheap and inexpensive. Cheap implies something flimsy that will easily break and fall apart. That's not an issue with these speakers. The materials they are made of are not high-end fancy, but they are not flimsy either. So let's call their construction inexpensive but not cheap.

There were two practical issues though, one trivial, one possibly a bit more problematic. The trivial issue is that the cord which connects the usb plug and speaker jack to your device has a very short connecting wire between the plug and the jack. For a phone or a laptop that is probably a non-issue. With my desktop though, I had to rearrange the usb plugs to open up one close enough to the speaker jack.

The issue which may be more of a hassle is that the volume controls are on the back of the sub-woofer. People usually tuck a sub-woofer away from easy reaching distance. So adjusting the volume may be a nuisance. Personally, I don't know why the volume controls aren't on the speakers which are usually more accessible. This may not be a big deal though if you can control the volume from your device. Just be aware of the possible hassle. In any event, our fifteen year old uses this speaker set to listen to music and movies on his laptop and he is happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: OROW S211 New USB-Powered 2.1 Multimedia Speakers System with Subwoofer,16W Computer Speakers,Strong Bass,3.5mm Audio Inputs,Great for PC/PS4/TV (Wooden)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black For the simple fact that this camera can do EVERYTHING I want it to do in my pocket, it get 5+ stars. I could go on for days about this camera, but I will try to hold this review to my personal game-changers.

HFR: Shooting video at 1080p, 120fps (100MB) and slowing down the footage in post produces better slow-mo videos compared to the HFR feature that can do 1080p 240fps at the best quality. The ultra HFR feature was a big sell for me, but I feel like 480fps and 960fps have garbage quality and it's really really difficult to get the timing right when you are taking the shot in that feature mode because you only have a 2 second timeframe. I must have spent 2 hours trying to get a slow-mo shot of a bee in my garden when I first bought it, but could never get the timing right on pressing record when the stupid bee would start flying. Shooting in normal video mode at 120fps and slowing down in post at 24fps is seriously amazing, and I will likely never use the HFR again.

Time-Lapse: Pay the $9.99 extra to download this app, because holy cow, it is freaking awesome. There is full manual control over intervals, # shots, etc, and it blows me away that it can produce day-night time-lapse with little to no flicker and amazing color with accurate white balance throughout. If you don't want the hassle of editing the stills in post, then you can just have the camera produce a 1080p 24fps video file in-camera, although post allows you more creativity and ability to produce 4k time lapse.
Slog2: I've been shooting all my videos in Slog2 (4k & 1080p) since I bought the camera several months ago, and up until just now I did not have a computer beefy enough to process the footage in post (which is the reason I have waited on posting my review). For the last week, I've been color grading my Slog2 footage with the Color Finale plugin in Final Cut Pro X. The footage is stunning and the dynamic range blows me away. I'm still trying to figure out the over exposure sweet spot of shooting in Slog2, but for the most part it looks really nice when shot at +1 - +2 stops over exposed and re-adjusted in post. There's not as much noise in the shadows as I expected, and I'm about to get the Neat Video Noise Reduction plugin that I expect to help with the little noise that I'm seeing. I went out to Joshua Tree for the meteor shower and shot 4k 24fps video of the stars, which is insane for a little camera like this.

Lens: Having the faster lens fully zoomed in (f2.8) compared to the RX100 M1's f4.9 is changed the way I take photos of my baby. It really was difficult to get a decent bokeh shooting at typical portrait focal lengths with the M1, but very easy now with the M4. Fast, clean and crisp, this lens is great.

Compact Size: I wanted a camera that I can put in my pocket. As long as you don't wear skinny jeans, then you're good to go. I don't wear skinny jeans, but I'm just saying. Cargos are the best, but then I realize that I've become the dad that wears cargos, and then I see the guy in Honduras swapping heavy lenses with a dslr around his neck and don't feel so bad. Although, I often worry when it's in my pocket that the lens ring control might bend and not be as smooth as it is, but that hasn't happened.

Focus Modes: Changing between focus modes is my one gripe about this camera. In a run and gun environment, I have not been able to figure out how to easily toggle between the various auto focus modes. It's easy to go between MF and AF, but trying to toggle between the AF modes when trying to get the right video clip of my active baby is extremely difficult. However, note that using the lens ring in AF mode for rack focusing is possible, which I wasn't able to do on the RX100 M1.

Overall, I wanted a camera that could do EVERYTHING, do everything WELL, and that EVERYTHING it does WELL could fit in my pocket….
text_fidelity_b: Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black

Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. My Toshiba windows 10 laptop came with DVD playing software and it doesn't even HAVE a dvd drive!

Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ROG GL552VW-DH74 15-Inch Gaming Laptop, Discrete GPU GeForce GTX 960M 4GB VRAM, 16GB DDR4, 1TB, 128GB SSD (ROG Metallic)

text_fidelity_a:
GAOMON PD1560 15.6 Inches 8192 Levels Pen Display with Arm Stand 1920 x 1080 HD IPS Screen Drawing Tablet with 10 Shortcut Keys TL:DR - if you want a good tablet from a brand that cares about it's customers/users AND has good drivers/software in a 16" screen you can't go wrong with this device. Huion Kamvas Pros are good and all, but I've heard too many issues compared to this device with virtually none. Especially considering the total cost is around 350 - 375.

It's not perfect and pickier users like me may not like some of the workarounds, but for a first art tablet that is basically what I'd consider the best package and/or intro into digital art you can't go wrong.

The GAOMON PD1560 really surprised me with it's performance to price ratio. The device itself is light weight and comes with what I would dub as a starter bundle of accessories. Tablet, Stand, Glove, Nibs, Carrying case, etc. The line quality is also really amazing and when running my tests didn't notice any abnormal line wobble if any at all. Brad Coblow does a good review of it. Contratry to his review the quality isn't bad at all. If you've handled a computer monitor this tablet feels like it more or less. Drivers weren't an issue and the hot keys were fantastic.

The pen kept a great charge and felt nice to use along with the included artist glove (I got only a single two finger one). Drawing without the screen protector was a little squeaky at times, but had no issue in CS6 and CSP. The tablet stays nearly completely when you adjust the brightness/backlit to sub 65 degrees F. Luckily it doesn't change the looks all that much. There is a bit of parallax and calibration can take some time to get completely right but pen accuracy is top notch.

Screen quality is good and the cables are pretty rigid so no worries there. They actually connect by recessing into a slot rather than on the edge of the device.

Lastly is customer service. I really enjoyed GAOMON's customer service which I wish more companies would do.

There are a few caveats though. To get the pen the most accurate no matter where you point on the screen you need to understand where you touch the dot when calibrating. Next you need to hold the pen in the exact same orientation and way when you draw. That means holding the pen the exact same way with little deviation of that angle to get things to line up as well as say an iPad Pro. If you don't the distance when you calibrate really well is under say... 0.5mm or less. I am really stingy about this, but for someone who isn't this isn't a big thing to worry about.

Next are the hotkeys which act more like a macbook's butterfly keyboard in terms of presses. They press well and have very little travel almost like the old iphone home buttons. This may bother some, but didn't for me. I did need to place some tape with texture to understand where my buttons were without looking.

The screen protector I didn't install and I found it really annoying to even attempt to install. Then again I've written with fountain pens for 5 years now so am very used to buttery smooth pen work.
text_fidelity_b: GAOMON PD1560 15.6 Inches 8192 Levels Pen Display with Arm Stand 1920 x 1080 HD IPS Screen Drawing Tablet with 10 Shortcut Keys

text_fidelity_a:
VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System Silver I wanted a set of speakers to use mainly for my Kindle Fire and MP3 player, but also as my computer speakers. Due to space constraints, a 2.0 system was my only option, since a subwoofer (regardless of the size) would be problematic.

So the search began. There were several speakers that sounded great, including the Creative Gigaworks, M Audio and Audioengine. However, they lacked the convenience features I wanted such as ease of connecting/disconnecting a tablet and volume control without having to reach out and touch the speaker.

The Bose Companion 20 initially caught my eye because of the control pod. That was a great solution to my problems since I could control the volume right on my desk plus have the ability to plug in/unplug a tablet very easily. The sound quality sealed the deal - everyone who hears these speakers think they are a 2.1 set due to the ample bass. But, the bass is not at the expense of clear mid and upper ranges.

I use these 60% for music and 40% for video, and for both applications, the sound quality has been just wonderful. I'm also impressed that they sound just as good with the volume dialed way down as they do at moderate or blast-out-the-walls loud.

The control pod is very well made. It has a nice weight to it and a non-skid backing so it stays put. The volume control works very smoothly with a solid feel. I'm especially fond of being able to turn the speakers on and off by just touching the control pod.

You can connect it to the PC and to an aux device (such as a tablet) and use both at the same time. That's important since I want to listen to music or a video from my Fire, but still want to hear a chime when an email arrives.

My complaints are that the control pod cable is a bit too short for my needs. It's about 5 foot long, which is ample if you have the speakers next to your PC, but I have my speakers on a shelf above my desk. I was able to arrange things to make it work, but another foot or two of cable (or the ability to purchase an extension) would have been nice. It's a custom cable, so an off-the-shelf extension is not possible.

My other complaint is the price. I was able to get a used pair for half of the regular price. I think these are a bit overpriced at the regular price. But, Bose hit a really unique niche - the ability to have great sound without any compromise in convenience. If you want both, there's a high cost for admission.

If the price is not an issue, these very much deserve a hard look if you're in the market for a great sounding pair of 2.0 speakers. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Once calibrated, this PC tablet works wonderfully. It is responsive to the stowable stylus or a tap of my fingernail, and I can even scroll with my thumb after adjusting the right edge width. The screen is sharp and clear, and it's speedy enough for pleasurable surfing and blog-reading, which is what I mostly want to use it for. I have not watched any HD movies on it yet, although the sample movie clip included with the computer shows what it's capable of...and it's gorgeous.

But I have a problem with the Archos 9. Because there is no fan, which makes for a very quiet experience, the lithium battery does get hot when held in your hands. Now, maybe there are people who will use this computer by pulling out the little easel-like stick in the back, but not me. I want to curl up on the sofa with it like a book. So I could see immediately that I wanted to rotate my Archos 9 PC Tablet's screen to portrait orientation so the battery would be at the top and not bother me so much. Well, doing so was a BIG mistake. Once you rotate the screen, it's pretty much impossible to recalibrate it; trying to move the cursor is like trying to walk without an inner ear: Directions ceased to make sense and I'd skew off East (or was it West?) when I meant to move North. It was all I could do to manage to restore the computer to its earlier state.

The little end piece of the easel-like appendage pulled off and I had to super-glue it back on, but that wasn't such a big deal. This appendage also stows into the back of the computer, and it can be pulled out short or long depending on whether you are watching a movie or trying to type on the on-screen keyboard. I can see it for watching a movie, but there's no way I'd ever try to type on the on-screen keyboard. Hunt-and-peck with the stylus is quicker. Needless to say, I will reach for my laptop if I have to do much typing.

I installed Skype, but it was too slow to show video unless I stopped everything else from running. This is fine with me, however, because I prefer to use Skype without the visuals. Google Chrome runs very well on it. I found I preferred the software keyboard (which you can drag around the screen) to the one that pops up when you press the keyboard key. I found that by keeping the former loaded and minimized to the tray, I can get around and do things online pretty efficiently. I just wish that battery didn't get so hot OR that I could easily/reliably rotate the screen to portrait. I gave this computer four stars because, on the whole, it's quite nice. But I must say that I am not likely to reach for the Archos 9 very often because of the discomfort from the battery heat when holding it in my hands. If they will come out with a software upgrade that will make screen rotation practical, then I will be a lot happier with this tablet PC.

A word to the wise: Immediately when you take your Archos 9 out of the box and get the software installed, you need to back it up. Don't wait a second longer than you have to. I was able to restore mine to its pristine newly installed state, but had I not backed it up, the whole thing would have been trashed by my little screen rotation exploit. You don't have a restore disk with this product. So be careful.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic SC-HC55 Compact Stereo System (Discontinued by Manufacturer) It's an attractive unit and has good sound. Features work well. Four stars on that basis. I got this primarily for listening to music and ballgames through my I phone, via bluetooth. I Tunes App available for this product. Worked okay.

Things I didn't like.
1. Not stable on the shelf. While trying to understand the controls, it fell backwards with a light touch. No damage though. If it's not wall mounted, suggest you place support behind it. I Was fiddling with the controls trying to find the pair button, since I couldn't find it on the remote. Later, I found the pair button on the remote. Should have better support for shelf use.
2. Remote control is confusing. Must be paired each time you want to play via bluetooth, even when you don't shut the unit down. Instead of a pair button, the button says play menu. The small pamphlet does explain the functions on the remote. Not intuitive at all. Read the pamphlet.
3. Paired to my I phone easily enough, once I hit the pair button (on the radio, as well as the remote).
4. Although it paired easily to my I Phone, my I mac couldn't find the signal.
5. Weak FM. A few stations were fine, but I only picked up about 1/3 of the stations available. Not a real problem since I will stream via bluetooth.
6. No AM. I expected AM.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic SC-HC55 Compact Stereo System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
